_conventions.text: Any text field may be a plain string or an object {"en": ..., "pt": ...}. Missing languages fall back to English. Proper nouns are never translated: non-Brazilian names stay in English, Brazilian names stay in Portuguese.
_conventions.dates: YYYY-MM or YYYY. "end": null means Present.
_conventions.tags: Controls where an item appears: "resume" (professional resume), "cv" (academic CV), "web" (website). Items without tags appear everywhere.
_conventions.private: Phone and other private fields live in data/private.json (gitignored) and are only merged into local PDF builds.

basics.name: Andre Assumpcao

label.en: Chief Data Strategist, National Center for State Courts (NCSC)
label.pt: Estrategista-Chefe de Dados, National Center for State Courts (NCSC)

basics.tagline: Supporting courts in their data journey

summary.en: I am the Chief Data Strategist at the National Center for State Courts (NCSC), where I contribute new data science tools (data dashboards, database management, predictive and causal inference) to the court community and NCSC's core products, and support courts in developing their AI and data strategies. Prior to the NCSC, I held research positions in government and think tanks, such as UNC's Criminal Justice Innovation Lab, the Center for International Development at the Harvard Kennedy School, the U.K. Foreign and Commonwealth Office, the Brookings Institution, and the Center of Politics and Public Economics (CEPESP-FGV).

education.institution: The University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill
The University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill
The University of Texas at Austin

work.summary: Support courts and the NCSC in developing their AI and data strategies, including partnerships with other branches of government, private companies, and non-profits.

highlights.text: Created more than three (3+) apps that integrate AI large language model solutions into data extraction tasks across the NCSC.
Created the NCSC Data Dives – an ongoing publication series covering topics around data collection, analysis, and presentation for state courts.
Led three (3) workshops (both internal and external) on potential uses of AI in state courts.
Led data collection and processing tasks for two (2) large federally funded state court criminal data projects.
Set up the infrastructure and implemented the NCSC's first large data warehouse.
Supported the development of data science skills across various teams at the NCSC with R and LLM training.

work.organization: Criminal Justice Innovation Lab (CJIL), UNC School of Government

highlights.text: Spearheaded the development of CJIL's Measuring Justice Data Dashboard with over thirty-five (35) criminal justice metrics across the entire state in under six (6) months.

Optimized CJIL's data analysis pipelines through the implementation of R and Python programs, reducing the time necessary to process state criminal case data from two (2) weeks to forty-eight (48) hours.

work.organization: Growth Lab, Center for International Development, Harvard University

highlights.text: Co-authored paper on changes of occupational tasks and implications for computerization and the gender pay gap.
Designed an algorithm to perform extractive summarization of long documents.
Managed two survey experiments for two applied research projects with over 15,000 respondents and co-authored paper on the factors determining Colombian migration.
Designed a data dashboard to report the results of one of the survey experiments in under thirty (30) days.

work.organization: University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill

highlights.text: Completed 5+ research projects (now submitted, under review, or accepted for publication).
Managed 5+ advisor-led research projects using experimental research methods.
Independently taught a graduate-level course on political economy of development and an undergraduate-level course on quantitative analysis of public policy.

work.organization: United Kingdom Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office

highlights.text: Secured a 6x increase in funding for finance and transparency projects during tenure (£50,000 to £300,000).
Organized 3 workshops on improving Brazil's financial sector.
Organized 5 Ministerial visits to / from the U.K. / Brazil.
Secured $200,000 worth of funding from national (National Council of Justice) and international organizations (Inter-American Development Bank) – equivalent to 5 years of ABJ's operational expenses.
Co-authored one paper on the landscape of tax (administrative) dispute resolution in Brazil and developed two data dashboards for external funders.
Conducted exploratory data analyses for the Metropolitan Policy Program.
Wrote 5+ analytical pieces for the Paris Global Competitiveness report.
Wrote independent grant application on the impact of immigration on human capital in U.S. metropolitan areas.
Designed and taught the IFRS Executive Education course on Financial Markets and Risks.

work.organization: Center for Politics and Economics of the Public Sector (CEPESP), FGV-EAESP

highlights.text: Managed large data collection initiative to build the most comprehensive database of federal transfers to municipalities to study public management and corruption.
Conducted statistical analysis for research paper on the governance of public health resources in Brazilian municipalities.

description.en: Analyzed Brazil's administrative tax litigation system, reviewing its effectiveness, institutional design, and key challenges across all levels of government.
description.pt: Analisou o sistema de contencioso administrativo tributário do Brasil, revisando sua eficácia, desenho institucional e principais desafios em todos os níveis de governo.

description.en: Applied natural language processing to analyze local government gazettes in Brazil.
description.pt: Aplicou processamento de linguagem natural para analisar diários oficiais de governos municipais no Brasil.

description.en: Structured the data feeding ABRAJI's portal containing all lawsuits filed against Brazilian politicians since 2014.
description.pt: Estruturou os dados do portal da ABRAJI contendo todos os processos judiciais movidos contra políticos brasileiros desde 2014.
